#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emits a divider glyph only when the given monitor's active workspace has
# open windows, so the divider disappears entirely (no reserved space)
# alongside the native workspace-taskbar icons when the workspace is empty.
set -euo pipefail
MONITOR="${1:-$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME}"

emit() {
  local ws count
  ws=$(hyprctl -j monitors | jq -r --arg m "$MONITOR" '.[] | select(.name == $m) | .activeWorkspace.id')
  count=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "${ws:-0}" '[ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) ] | length')
  if [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    jq -nc '{text: "│"}'
  else
    jq -nc '{text: ""}'
  fi
}

emit

socat -U - "UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock" | \
while read -r line; do
  case "$line" in
    openwindow*|closewindow*|movewindow*|workspace*|activewindow*|focusedmon*)
      emit
      ;;
  esac
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emits waybar JSON selecting a pikachu sprite via CSS class. The sprite itself
# lives in style.css as a background-image on #custom-battery-icon.<class>.
set -euo pipefail

BATTERY_SYSFS="${BATTERY_SYSFS:-/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/capacity}"

log() {
  printf '[%s] pickachu-battery: %s\n' "$(date -Iseconds)" "$*" >&2
}

# A single space, not an empty string: waybar hides a custom module whose text
# is empty, and the space is what the background image paints behind.
emit() {
  printf '{"text":"%s","class":"%s"}\n' "$1" "$2"
}

capacity="${WAYBAR_BATTERY_CAPACITY:-}"

if [ -z "$capacity" ]; then
  if [ ! -r "$BATTERY_SYSFS" ]; then
    log "cannot read $BATTERY_SYSFS; hiding module"
    emit "" ""
    exit 0
  fi
  capacity=$(<"$BATTERY_SYSFS")
fi

if ! [[ "$capacity" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  log "non-numeric capacity '$capacity'; hiding module"
  emit "" ""
  exit 0
fi

if [ "$capacity" -gt 80 ]; then
  class=p100
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 60 ]; then
  class=p80
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 40 ]; then
  class=p60
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 20 ]; then
  class=p40
elif [ "$capacity" -gt 10 ]; then
  class=p20
else
  class=p10
fi

log "capacity=$capacity class=$class"
emit " " "$class"

I have everything needed. Here is the full picture.

## Summary

The "pokeball" is not a module at all — it is a pure-CSS background image painted onto the **active workspace button** of the `hyprland/workspaces` module. There is no pokeball script, no signal, no interval. It moves purely because Waybar's workspaces module re-applies the `.active` CSS class as Hyprland's focused workspace changes.

## 1. The pokeball definition

It lives entirely in CSS, not in `config.jsonc`.

`/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css` (lines 29-44):
```css
/* :not(.taskbar) keeps this off the taskbar module's active button */
#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active {
    background-image: url('/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pokeball.png');
    background-position: center;
    background-repeat: no-repeat;
    background-size: contain;
    background-origin: content-box;
    background-color: @primary;
    color: transparent; /* hides the workspace number behind the pokeball */
    padding: 4px 4px;
    margin: 4px 0px;
    min-width: 20px;
    min-height: 20px;
    border: 1px solid @outline;
    border-radius: 10px;
}
```

The asset is `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pokeball.png` (598 bytes). The rule targets any `button.active` inside a `#workspaces` element that does **not** also carry the `.taskbar` class — so it applies to the main workspaces module but is deliberately excluded from the second workspaces#taskbar module.

The relevant module in `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/config.jsonc` (lines 27-33) is the plain workspaces module — it has no pokeball reference itself; the pokeball is added by CSS on whichever button is `.active`:
```jsonc
"hyprland/workspaces": {
    "format": "{name}",
    "all-outputs": true,
    "ignore-hidden": false,
    "on-click": "activate",
    "tooltip": false
},
```

Note `modules-center` (line 11-15) contains two workspaces modules: `"hyprland/workspaces"` (the pokeball one) and `"hyprland/workspaces#taskbar"` (line 47-60, which has `all-outputs: false`, `active-only: true`, renders window icons, and is CSS-excluded from the pokeball via `.taskbar`).

## 2. Scripts

The two scripts under `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/` are **unrelated to the pokeball**:

- `pickachu-battery.sh` — drives the battery icon (`custom/battery-icon`); emits a CSS class `p10`…`p100` selecting a pikachu sprite. Not pokeball-related.
- `workspace-tabs.sh` — drives the `custom/taskbar-divider` module. This one IS relevant to your per-monitor goal because it demonstrates the pattern you'll need. Full content:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
MONITOR="${1:-$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME}"

emit() {
  local ws count
  ws=$(hyprctl -j monitors | jq -r --arg m "$MONITOR" '.[] | select(.name == $m) | .activeWorkspace.id')
  count=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "${ws:-0}" '[ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) ] | length')
  if [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    jq -nc '{text: "│"}'
  else
    jq -nc '{text: ""}'
  fi
}

emit
socat -U - "UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock" | \
while read -r line; do
  case "$line" in
    openwindow*|closewindow*|movewindow*|workspace*|activewindow*|focusedmon*)
      emit
      ;;
  esac
done
```
Key takeaway: this script already reads **`$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME`** (the per-bar output name Waybar injects into each instance) and subscribes to Hyprland's **socket2** event stream to react per-monitor. This is exactly the mechanism you'd replicate for a per-monitor pokeball.

## 3. How Waybar is launched — one instance, one bar per monitor

Waybar is launched **once**, with no per-output config, from `/home/krubics/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` (line 54-59):
```lua
hl.on("hyprland.start", function()
     hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_cmd("/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libexec/polkit-kde-authentication-agent-1"))
     hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_cmd("yin"))
     hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_cmd("yinctl --image /home/krubics/.config/hypr/images/latios-latias.jpg"))
     hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_cmd("waybar"))
end)
```
There is no systemd user unit for waybar, no `output` field anywhere in `config.jsonc`, and no `--config`/`--output` flags. Because a single Waybar config has no `"output"` key, **Waybar renders one identical bar on every monitor** (here: `eDP-1` and `HDMI-A-1`). Each of those bar instances gets its own `$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME`, but they all share the same JSONC/CSS.

Toggle bind exists in `/home/krubics/.config/hypr/conf/keybinds.lua` line 123: `pkill -SIGUSR1 waybar` (SUPER+SHIFT+SPACE) — global toggle, not per-monitor.

## 4. How the pokeball currently updates

Mechanism: **none custom** — it is Waybar's built-in `hyprland/workspaces` behavior. Waybar listens to Hyprland's socket2 internally and toggles the `.active` CSS class on the button of the focused workspace; the CSS rule then paints the pokeball there. No SIGRTMIN, no `interval`, no script.

The crucial limitation for your goal: the module has **`"all-outputs": true`**. That means every bar (on both monitors) shows the same full set of workspaces, and Waybar marks the button `.active` for the single **globally focused** workspace. So today **both monitors' bars show the pokeball on the same workspace button** — the one focused workspace — regardless of which workspace is visible on the other monitor. There is only one `.active` at a time across all bars. (Waybar does also apply a `.visible` class to workspaces currently displayed on a monitor, but the CSS only styles `.active`.)

## 5. Monitor + workspace binding

Monitors are defined in `/home/krubics/.config/hypr/hyprland-gui.lua` (required at the top of hyprland.lua via `require("hyprland-gui")`):
```lua
hl.monitor({ output = "HDMI-A-1", disabled = false, mode = "2560x1440@144.00Hz", position = "2580x210", scale = 1, cm = "srgb" })
hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1",    disabled = false, mode = "2560x1440@165.00Hz", position = "20x210",   scale = 1, cm = "srgb" })
```
`hyprland.lua` also has a generic `hl.monitor({ output="", mode="preferred", ... })` fallback (lines 26-31) and lid-switch binds that disable/enable `eDP-1` (lines 246-253).

Workspace-to-monitor binding: there are **no static `workspace = ... , monitor = ...` rules**. Workspaces are not pinned to monitors. They're assigned dynamically. Workspace keybinds are in `/home/krubics/.config/hypr/conf/keybinds.lua` (lines 98-105):
```lua
for i = 1, 9 do
    hl.bind(modKey .. " + " .. i, hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = i }))
    hl.bind(modKey .. " + SHIFT + " .. i, hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = i }))
    hl.bind(modKey .. " + SHIFT + ALT + " .. i, hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = i, silent = true }))
end
```
Since Hyprland assigns each workspace to whichever monitor is focused when first opened, each monitor has its own `activeWorkspace` (queryable via `hyprctl -j monitors | jq '.[] | {name, activeWorkspace}'`).

## How the pieces connect / planning notes for a per-monitor pokeball

- The pokeball is a CSS `background-image` on `#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active` in `style.css`. There is exactly one `.active` button per bar as Waybar sees it, but with `all-outputs: true` all bars agree on the same globally focused workspace.
- To make it independent per monitor you have two realistic routes:
  1. **Set `"all-outputs": false`** on `"hyprland/workspaces"` so each bar only shows its own monitor's workspaces and marks its own visible/active workspace. Then the existing `button.active` CSS would naturally show a pokeball per monitor. (This mirrors how `hyprland/workspaces#taskbar` already uses `all-outputs: false`.) Waybar also exposes a `.visible` class you could target if you want to highlight the workspace visible on each specific monitor rather than the globally focused one.
  2. **A custom module per output** (like `workspace-tabs.sh`): read `$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME`, query `hyprctl -j monitors` for that monitor's `activeWorkspace.id`, subscribe to socket2 (`focusedmon`, `workspace`, `activewindow` events), and emit a class Waybar maps to the pokeball background. This is the pattern already proven in `workspace-tabs.sh`.
- Waybar is a single shared process rendering one bar per monitor; each bar instance carries a distinct `$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME`, which is the hook any per-monitor logic must use.
- Monitors (`eDP-1`, `HDMI-A-1`) are defined in `hyprland-gui.lua`; no workspace is statically bound to a monitor, so per-monitor active workspace must be read at runtime from `hyprctl -j monitors`.

Relevant files (all absolute):
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/config.jsonc`
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/style.css`
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/assets/pokeball.png`
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/workspace-tabs.sh`
- `/home/krubics/.config/waybar/scripts/pickachu-battery.sh`
- `/home/krubics/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`

- `/home/krubics/.config/hypr/conf/keybinds.lua`
